description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by the s473t6c review probe for #1921; PRE-EXISTING on main c7f89fa8 and UNCHANGED by #1921 (that fix repairs the quote token's SECTION RECORD; this is the rename FIXER's own matching, and it shows in a plain "..." string, which has no section record).

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/t6c/adj1.pl, p-adjacent3.pl):
  { my $v = 1; print "inner $v\n"; }        # an inner-block declaration of the SAME name: gives the rename a region
  my $v = 7;
  sub f { print "A[$v$v]\n" }  f();          # a sub reading the file-level one: identity-promoted -> $v__file__N
  perl: A[77]     PCL (main and the t6c tree): A[7]
Same in a substitution's replacement (`s/a/[$v$v]/` -> `[7]`) and its pattern (`s/$v$v/no/` on "7x7": perl no match, PCL matches one `7`).  `"$dir$file|$file$dir|$dir/$file"` are all RIGHT; only `$dir$dir` loses one.  `"$v-$v"`, `"$v $v"`, `"$v\$v"` are right.

THE SUSPECT, with its cheap discriminating measurement (NOT taken): the fixer closure built in Pl/Parser2.pm (the `_interp_fixer` family, the one `_fix_interp_token` applies) matches a name with a CONSUMED left-context character (a guard against an escaped sigil), so under /g the second adjacent occurrence's left context is the END of the first match and is never seen.  Measurement: dump the closure's regex and run it over the literal text `A[$v$v]` -- one substitution = confirmed; the fix is a lookbehind instead of a consumed group.  If it is NOT that, print the token content before and after `_fix_interp_token`.

SECOND FINDING, LOUD not silent: the braced spelling under the same rename -- `sub f { print "C[${v}$v]\n" }` -- refuses the WHOLE FILE: "Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'v' captured by sub f" (also `"${dir}${file}"`).  So the fixer knows it cannot rewrite the braced form and declines by refusing.  The braced form is everyday Perl (`"${prefix}_suffix"`), and the refusal needs BOTH an inner-block redeclaration and a sub capture, which is why the corpus has not met it.  Standing rule (memory): "a SIGIL- or SCOPE-blind capture refusal is a BUG -- delete/rename, never narrow"; and interpolation scanning happens in Pl/InterpScan.pm or not at all -- the right fix routes the rename through InterpScan's variable EVENTS (which already know the braced, array, element and hash-element spellings) instead of a regex over the token text.

BAR: Pl/ name-resolution / rename change -> THE FULL SWEEP IS THE GATE (#296), corpus-diff, emission A/B, gate-SET scan over BOTH populations (a refusal stops firing), `--quick` companion once; guard rows in Pl/t/interp-rename-sections-01.t (the #1921 file: it already carries the rename fixture).

=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED 383821a1.  THE TASK'S OWN DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, taken first: the
closure's regex run over `A[$v$v]` makes ONE substitution.  `_interp_fixer`'s
escape guard CONSUMED the character to the left of the sigil --
`((?:^|[^\\])(?:\\\\)*)` -- so under /g the second of two adjacent occurrences
had its left context eaten by the first match and was never seen.  `"A[$v$v]"`
printed `A[7]` where perl prints `A[77]`, silently, under an ordinary rename;
both sides of an s/// lost one the same way, so `s/$v$v/no/` on "7x7" MATCHED
where perl does not.

The guard is now the zero-width `(?<!\\)((?:\\\\)*)`, which says exactly the
same thing (an EVEN number of backslashes immediately before the sigil) without
consuming anything.  All eleven patterns in the closure take it; the shape
occurs nowhere else in Pl/ (grepped), so this is the one place.

Twelve shapes probed vs perl 5.40.3, identical after
(scratch/s492a/probes/m6-family.{pl,perl.out,base.out,tree.out}): `$v$v`,
`$v$v$v`, `@a@a`, `$#a$#a`, an s/// replacement and both pattern directions,
`$a[0]$a[1]`, a separated pair, an escaped sigil, an escaped backslash, and
`@{[ ... ]}$v`.

Guard: 10 rows in Pl/t/interp-rename-sections-01.t (8 -> 18), ONE program per
SBCL launch.  On a 268d7e00 extraction rows 9-14 FAIL and 15-18 -- the
separated pair, the escaped sigil, the escaped backslash and the control --
pass (scratch/s492a/inverse-guards-base268.log).

THE BRACED SPELLING, measured as the task asked: `"${v}$v"` under the same
rename still refuses the WHOLE FILE, and this fix does not reach it -- that is
the CAPTURE check, not the fixer.  FILED as #2014 with the InterpScan-events
shape.  No refusal stopped firing here, so no gate-SET scan was owed for this
member.
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare shape, pre-existing): the SAME renamed variable twice in a row in an interpolating string loses one occurrence -- `"$dir$dir"` prints `/tmp` (perl `/tmp/tmp`) when `$dir` is a file lexical that gets RENAMED (an inner-block `my $dir` + a sub reading the file-level one); two DIFFERENT adjacent names are fine; the braced spelling `"${dir}"` is a whole-file refusal instead
